title: Compact observability for edge deployments
content:
Purpose and context:
This note captures a lightweight observability pattern for Redwood deployments that run closer to users (mobile-edge nodes, partner PoPs, and private edge racks). The goal: keep investigation velocity high for incidents while minimizing telemetry volume and dashboard complexity for low-bandwidth/low-cost environments. This is intended as a pragmatic guide for product owners, runtime engineers, and SREs responsible for private/edge flavors of Redwood Private and Dedicated.

Design principles (compact-first):
- Minimal telemetry surface: collect the smallest set of signals that reliably distinguish common failure modes (cold-starts, KV cache misses, quantization degradation, network egress issues).
- Tiered fidelity: default to lightweight aggregates; enable higher-fidelity traces/metrics for a tenant or time window on demand.
- Cost-awareness: prefer counters and coarse histograms over high-cardinality labels; offload expensive traces to sampling windows triggered by anomaly detectors.
- Investigate-in-place: dashboards should enable quick triage without expanding to many panels; each tile should answer one hypothesis.
- Consistent naming: metric and span names follow a compact, stable convention to simplify cross-environment tooling.

Core signals to capture (minimal set):
- redwood.inference.requests.count (counter) — labels: tenant_id, model_variant, region, outcome (success,error,timeout)
- redwood.inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 (histogram or summary) — labels: model_variant, region, seq_len_bucket
- redwood.inference.tokens.per_request.p50/p95 (summary) — labels: model_variant
- redwood.inference.kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge, percent) — labels: model_variant, region
- redwood.inference.batch.size.p50 (summary) — labels: model_variant
- redwood.inference.cost.per_1k_tokens (derived gauge) — labels: model_variant, quantization
- redwood.inference.errors.by_type (counter) — labels: error_type, model_variant
- redwood.inference.network.egress_ms (histogram) — labels: region, upstream_host

Cardinality guidance and label hygiene:
- Avoid free-form user ids at the metric label level. Use tenant_id only when absolutely necessary and rool up to tenant_tier when possible.
- Model_variant should be a small enumerated set (e.g., rwd-3b, llama-70b-8q, rwd-emerald-v2). Do NOT attach git commit SHAs or full model hashes.
- Quantization label: {fp16, int8, int4} — keep it low-cardinality.
- seq_len_bucket: fixed buckets e.g. tiny(0-64), short(65-256), medium(257-1024), long(1025+) — used in latency panels instead of raw seq length.

Adaptive trace sampling approach (edge-friendly):
1) Default: sample 1 in 2000 full request traces at the edge cluster level. Instrumentation emits small span metadata for every request (no body, token-level details stripped) so we still get path coverage.
2) Microtraces (always-on): emit a compact single-span event per request containing: span_id, duration_ms, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, cache_hit (bool), batch_size, outcome. These are cheap and retained longer for rollups.
3) On-demand ramp: when the lightweight anomaly rules trigger (see alerts below), temporarily increase full-trace sampling to 1 in 10 for affected tenant/model/region for 5–15 minutes. Ramp down automatically.
4) Privacy and size: traces must never include full prompts or responses; only structural metadata allowed. On private deployments we emit a tenant-hash instead of tenant_id.

Compact dashboard layout (single-screen triage for edge):
Row A (health strip, one row of small panels):
- Request count delta (1m/5m/1h) — heatmap style
- Error rate (% by outcome) — stacked area
- Cost-per-1k-tokens (rolling 1h) — sparkline
- KV cache hit ratio (rolling 1h) — sparkline

Row B (latency and capacity):
- Latency distribution by seq_len_bucket (stacked small multiples) — p50/p95 for each bucket
- Batch size distribution (histogram) with target overlay (helps detect batching issues)
- Active workers / GPU utilization (single gauge per cluster)

Row C (top-n investigative panels):
- Top 5 error_types with sample links to traces
- Top 10 tenants by token usage (with tenant_tier) — click-to-isolate
- Recent trace waterfall for the sampled window (compact)

Panel design notes:
- Every panel must be readable on a 1366x768 screen without horizontal scroll.
- Drill-through: panels link directly to the raw trace or request log with pre-applied filters.
- Export small CSVs from panels for quick offline analysis (edge sites may have flaky UI bandwidth).

Alerting rules (compact & robust):
- Alert A (Cost spike): token-cost-per-1k increases >20% vs baseline (rolling 3h vs 7d same time) for a model_variant — severity: p2.
- Alert B (Degraded latency): p95 latency for short bucket > SLO_threshold for 5m and request volume > 5rps — severity: p1.
- Alert C (KV cache miss storm): cache hit ratio drops > 30% absolute in 2m window AND error rate increases > 1% — severity: p1.
- Alert D (Network egress tail): 99th network.egress_ms increases by >3x for region — severity: p2.
- Anti-flapping: require condition to persist for at least two buckets (default buckets: 60s) and suppress duplicate notifications for 15m per alert key.

Investigation playbook (first 7 min):
1) Confirm scope in the health strip: which region/model/tenant is affected?
2) Check KV cache hit ratio and batch size distribution. If cache hit dropped and errors rose, suspect cache invalidation or mismatch in model variant.
3) Open recent sampled traces (use the on-demand ramp links) and look for repeated span patterns: repeated model-load spans, repeated retry spans, or large network.egress spans.
4) If traces show many small batches (batch_size << target), check ingress proxy or batching-worker backpressure metrics.
5) If cost-per-1k spikes without latency changes, investigate quantization fallback or fallback to larger variant.

Instrumentation checklist for runtime engineers (practical):
- Emit the microtrace single-span event for every request. Keep size < 900 bytes.
- Add seq_len_bucket, quantization, cache_hit, batch_size as top-level attributes on spans and microtrace events.
- Ensure SDK/agents redact user content before leaving process boundary.
- Provide an environment toggle to emit tenant-hash in private deployments.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Start with a single edge-region pilot (e.g., eu-west-edge-1) and run compact dashboards in parallel with full-fidelity dashboards for 2 weeks to compare signal fidelity.
- Tune sampling multiplier for the on-demand ramp based on observed noise; aim for < 0.01% increase in overall trace volume when ramping.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Decide retention policy: microtraces 90 days? aggregated histograms 365 days? (privacy considerations push shorter retention on private installs).
- Evaluate lightweight local storage of high-fidelity traces for 24 hours at edge nodes (flush to central store on demand).
- Build a small UI widget to request on-demand ramp from the dashboard with one click (blocked on auth scoping).

Appendix: example metric name conventions (compact):
- redwood.inference.requests.count{region,model_variant,tenant_tier,outcome}
- redwood.inference.latency_ms{region,model_variant,seq_len_bucket}.p95
- redwood.inference.kv_cache.hit_ratio{region,model_variant}
- redwood.inference.trace.micro{region,model_variant,cache_hit,batch_size}

Notes: This is intentionally pragmatic and conservative in signal count. The objective is to make edge deployments debuggable with limited telemetry. Feedback requested from: serving-runtime, private-deployments, and SRE teams — especially on retention, tenant labeling, and the microtrace schema.
